pages_detail.activities: Child reads the story about Maya and Ana, circles the word that tells what Maya is like (shy, kind, angry), then circles the action from the story that shows Maya is kind, from three story sentences. No word bank. Supported.
answers: Action: 'Maya shares her crayons with Ana.'
pages_detail.title: What Is Maya Like?

pages_detail.activities: Child reads the story about Theo and the puzzle, then writes how Theo feels when the piece will not fit, what he does that shows how he feels, and how he feels at the end when he smiles. No word bank; the feelings are never named in the text. Guided.
answers: He frowns (accept: he pushes the piece hard)
pages_detail.title: How Does Theo Feel?

pages_detail.activities: Child reads the story about the red mitten, writes why Theo says to put it in the lost and found box, circles the word that tells what Theo is like (responsible, greedy, silly), then explains what the choice shows about Theo. The two explanations each get two full writing lines. Guided.
answers: Theo says that because the mitten belongs to someone (accept: because it is not theirs)
Theo is responsible because he puts the mitten where its owner can find it (accept: because he does the right thing with something that is not his)
pages_detail.title: Why Does Theo Make That Choice?

pages_detail.activities: Child reads the story about Maya reading to the class, fills two boxes for how Maya feels at the start and at the end, using a feeling word bank (scared, nervous, happy, proud), then explains what changes how she feels. Guided.
answers: At the start, Maya feels scared (accept: nervous)
At the end, Maya feels proud (accept: happy)
Maya feels better because she reads her story and the class claps (accept: because Theo tells her she can do it, or because she does it)
pages_detail.title: How Does Maya Feel?

pages_detail.activities: Child reads the story about the rainy picnic, writes what the problem is and what Theo does on open lines (two lines each), then names the trait (flexible, from a word bank with creative) and explains how Theo's response shows it, with two full writing lines. Word bank only (rain, inside, blanket, friend, flexible, creative). No sentence starters. Independent.
answers: The rain falls (accept: the picnic is ruined)
He says they can have the picnic inside (accept: he finds a new way)
Theo is flexible because he changes the plan and has the picnic inside (accept: creative, because he thinks of a new way; or because he does not give up on the picnic)
pages_detail.title: Theo Meets a Challenge
